## Topic

I chose three books about the mathematical and statistical foundations of data science. For each book, I will use the title, authors, publication year, publisher, and ISBN. All three books have more than one author.

## Files

I will create the same records in two formats:

- `books.html`, using an HTML table
- `books.json`, using an array of JSON objects

I will enter the files by hand so I can practice the structure of each format.

## R process

I will use `rvest` to read the HTML table and `jsonlite` to read the JSON file. After importing the files, I will check the number of rows and columns, column names, and data types.

Before using `identical()`, I will put the columns in the same order. I will also make Year an integer and ISBN a character field in both data frames. ISBN is an identifier, so it should not be used as a numeric value.

## Checks

I will check for missing values and duplicate rows. I will also test the ISBN-13 check digits. The ISBN test only checks whether the number follows the ISBN-13 formula. It does not confirm the book title or edition.

## Expected issue

HTML and JSON may import the same value with different data types. If the data frames look the same but `identical()` returns `FALSE`, I will check their structure before changing any values.

I will check the book information against the publishers' pages before I finish the files.

## Expected result

I expect both files to produce data frames with three rows and five columns. After the column order and types are consistent, I expect the two data frames to match.
